findings.title: Louvain community degrees never re-aggregated after label moves
findings.description: In relaxedCommunities, communityDegrees is initialized as a copy of per-node degrees ([...degrees]) and indexed by community label. This only works while every node is its own community. As nodes move (labels[index] = best), the degree bookkeeping uses `communityDegrees[current] -= degrees[index]` and `communityDegrees[best] += degrees[index]`, which is correct incrementally — but the modularity gain formula compares against `communityDegrees[candidate]` where `candidate` iterates over neighbor labels including `current` after the node was already removed. The subtle bug: when evaluating `current` as a candidate inside the loop, the gain computed for `current` in the loop uses the already-decremented total (correct), but `bestGain` was seeded with the same value before the loop, so `current` is evaluated twice — harmless. The real issue is that the pass loop cap `Math.min(count * 2, 20)` combined with single-level Louvain (no graph coarsening/second phase) means large components may not converge; labels are used directly as community ids without compaction, and there is no aggregation phase, so this is only a local-move heuristic. If that is intentional, document it; otherwise results can be order-dependent for graphs needing more than 20 passes.
findings.suggestedFix: Either document that this is a single-level local-moving heuristic (not full Louvain) and that the 20-pass cap can leave the partition unconverged, or detect non-convergence (moved === true after the final pass) and log/handle it deterministically.

findings.title: mergeAnchoredCommunities mutates shared cluster objects during iteration
findings.description: After merging (`target.groups.push(...candidate.groups)`), the candidate cluster is spliced out but the merged `target` keeps `corroborated` from before the merge and its groups grow. `conceptAnchors` and `clustersAreCompatible` are recomputed each iteration against the mutated target, which is fine, but the removed candidate object is not emptied — if any external reference to it exists (e.g., in `mergeCorroboratedLocationClusters`, clusters are the same object instances passed into `mergeAnchoredCommunities`), the original array in the caller still holds the pre-splice cluster with its groups now duplicated inside target. In mergeCorroboratedLocationClusters the final `mergeAnchoredCommunities(clusters.filter(...))` operates on a copy of the array but the same cluster objects; a cluster absorbed there remains in scope. Because the function returns `remaining`, the duplicates don't currently leak, but the merged-cluster's groups now appear in two live cluster objects, which is fragile and will silently duplicate findings if the return value handling ever changes.
findings.suggestedFix: After `target.groups.push(...candidate.groups)`, also set `candidate.groups = []` (as done in the attachment loop) so the absorbed cluster cannot resurface with duplicated members.

findings.title: O(n^3+) restart-on-merge loop with full re-sort per merge
findings.description: mergeAnchoredCommunities re-sorts the entire `remaining` array and restarts the double loop from scratch (`break outer` plus `while (merged)`) after every single merge. Each compatibility check itself is quadratic in member counts (clustersAreCompatible does every-vs-every over groups and members, and conceptAnchors is recomputed for the same target repeatedly across inner iterations). For large components at the same location this is potentially O(n^3 · m^2) and can become a hot spot. The repeated `remaining.sort(...)` after splice is also unnecessary — splice preserves order.
findings.suggestedFix: Drop the re-sort after splice (order is already maintained), cache conceptAnchors per cluster and invalidate on merge, and continue scanning from the current position instead of restarting the outer while-loop.

findings.title: attachmentEvidence support Math.min over empty-fix members can zero out valid attachments
findings.description: In mergeCorroboratedLocationClusters, `support: Math.min(...supports)` requires EVERY member of a multi-member fringe candidate to independently meet the anchor/fix-support gate in attachmentEvidence. attachmentEvidence returns {support: 0} whenever `anchorCount < 2 && !(anchorCount === 1 && fixSupport >= 2)`. A candidate with one strongly-matching member and one member with a terse title/description will therefore never attach, even when the cluster as a whole is clearly the same concept. This is stated as intentional in the comment ("absorbed only when every member supports the same target"), but the interaction with fixSupport — which requires suggestedFix similarity, a frequently-absent optional field — makes the gate stricter than the comment implies. Findings without a suggestedFix can never satisfy the anchorCount===1 escape hatch.
findings.suggestedFix: Consider allowing description similarity as an alternative to suggestedFix similarity in the fixSupport computation, or document that single-anchor attachment requires the optional suggestedFix field to be present.

findings.title: relaxedEdgeDensity computed against pre-community-pruning indexes map keyed by array identity
findings.description: `relaxedEdgeDensity(component, indexes, adjacency)` looks up group indexes via a Map keyed by TaggedFinding[] array identity. This works only because splitCompatibleChains and connectedComponents preserve the exact array references from `groups`. If any intermediate step ever copies a group array (e.g., a future refactor using .map or spread on a group), the `indexes.get(...)!` non-null assertion will throw at runtime with an opaque error. The double non-null assertion `adjacency[indexes.get(groups[i]!)!]!` hides this fragility.
findings.suggestedFix: Carry the original index alongside each group (e.g., tuple of {group, index}) through splitCompatibleChains/connectedComponents instead of relying on object identity in a Map, or add an explicit guard with a descriptive error.

findings.title: groupsShareLocation uses every-vs-every, making cluster compatibility non-monotonic
findings.description: groupsShareLocation requires EVERY pair across two groups to be same-file and line-overlapping. clustersAreCompatible then requires this for every group pair. As clusters grow via merges in mergeAnchoredCommunities and the attachment loop, previously-compatible pairs can become incompatible depending on merge order (a cluster that absorbed a fringe member with slightly different lines may now fail overlap against a third cluster). Combined with the greedy first-match `clusters.find(...)` in splitCompatibleChains, the final partition depends on the deterministic-but-arbitrary sort order rather than an optimal grouping. The determinism test only checks review-order invariance, not that the grouping is stable under small line perturbations.
findings.suggestedFix: Document the order-dependence, or use a representative span (min start / max end) per cluster for overlap checks so compatibility is monotonic under merges.

findings.title: Hardcoded domain-specific stopwords mixed with generic ones
findings.description: CORROBORATION_STOPWORDS embeds domain-ish tokens like 'config', 'configuration', 'generated', 'test', 'tests' directly into the deduper. These meaningfully change merge behavior (e.g., two findings about test configuration lose those anchors) and are calibrated against one corpus (RCL-17). They are neither configurable nor referenced by the calibration docs.
findings.suggestedFix: Extract the added stopwords to a named, documented constant (e.g., REVIEW_DOMAIN_STOPWORDS) with a comment tying each addition to the corpus evidence, or make them configurable alongside the thresholds.

findings.title: Regex claim-kind patterns are brittle and Elixir-specific
findings.description: TYPE_CONTRACT_PATTERN, GLOBAL_LOG_CAPTURE_PATTERN etc. hardcode Elixir/corpus-specific vocabulary (@spec, typespec, capture_log). compatibleClaimKinds tests only the title, not description/fix. A finding titled generically ('Return value not reflected in signature') but describing a typespec issue in its body will be classified as compatible with runtime findings, re-opening the exact bridge the comment in relaxedLocationDuplicate warns about. Also, `\bn\s*\+\s*1\b` in PERFORMANCE_CONTRACT_PATTERN will match arithmetic like 'n + 1 retries' in unrelated titles and flip compatibility.
findings.suggestedFix: Test the patterns against title + description (or at least document why title-only), and tighten the N+1 pattern (e.g., /\bn\s*\+\s*1\s*(quer|select|problem)/i).

findings.title: Attachment rounds cap uses clusters.length, not intended constant semantics
findings.description: The loop bound `Math.min(clusters.length, CORROBORATED_MAX_ATTACHMENT_ROUNDS)` means that when there is exactly 1 cluster, one round still runs (fine), but the constant's comment says it bounds 'transitive fringe growth' to 2 rounds. Because attachments within a round are applied against frozen state but candidate.groups is emptied (candidate.groups = []) while the cluster object stays in `clusters`, subsequent rounds iterate over empty clusters and `candidateMembers.length === 0` skips them — correct but wasteful. More importantly, an attached fringe cluster's members are added to target.groups but target.corroborated is never recomputed, and evidence from newly-attached members in round 2 comes from clusters whose distinctReviewers may now exceed thresholds without re-validation of density.
findings.suggestedFix: Filter emptied clusters out of the iteration set between rounds, and consider recomputing or explicitly documenting that corroborated status is intentionally frozen after the core pass.

findings.title: collapseSameReviewer applied twice to the same members
findings.description: strictGroups are built with collapseSameReviewer(coherent), then after mergeCorroboratedLocationClusters the result maps each merged member list through collapseSameReviewer again. The second pass is necessary for merged clusters (members from different strict groups may share a reviewer) but redundant for unmerged singleton groups. Harmless if collapseSameReviewer is idempotent, but that invariant is implicit; if it ever selects differently on second application (e.g., tie-breaking on group order), representatives could shift versus the pre-change behavior.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a comment noting collapseSameReviewer must be idempotent, or only re-collapse groups whose membership changed during mergeCorroboratedLocationClusters.

findings.title: agreementClusterKey padStart(10) fails for negative or >10-digit line numbers
findings.description: String(finding.startLine).padStart(10, '0') produces incorrect lexicographic ordering for negative line numbers ('-5' pads to '00000000-5') and for hypothetical values over 10 digits. Line numbers should never be negative, but the deduper does not validate inputs, and a malformed finding would silently destabilize the deterministic ordering this key exists to guarantee.
findings.suggestedFix: Clamp with Math.max(0, line) before padding, or compare numerically in compareAgreementClusters instead of building a composite string.

findings.title: compatibleClaimKinds concept check inverts vacuously when one side has no concepts
findings.description: The final return treats findings as compatible whenever either side has zero extracted concepts (conceptsA.size === 0 || conceptsB.size === 0 makes the negated condition true). This means a finding with recognizable concepts can merge with a vaguely-worded finding that extracted none, even though the regex-pattern gates above use strict equality of matches. The asymmetry (patterns: both-or-neither; concepts: overlap-or-either-empty) is undocumented and easy to misread due to the negated boolean expression.
findings.suggestedFix: Rewrite for clarity: `if (conceptsA.size === 0 || conceptsB.size === 0) return true; return [...conceptsA].some((c) => conceptsB.has(c));` and add a comment justifying the vacuous-compatibility choice.

findings.title: CORROBORATED_TIE_EPSILON declared but tie logic mixes it with exact equality
findings.description: The tie-break guard in the attachment ranking uses exact equality for support and size but CORROBORATED_TIE_EPSILON only for strength. Meanwhile relaxedCommunities uses Number.EPSILON for its own tie comparisons. Two different epsilon conventions in the same file for floating-point tie detection invites drift; Number.EPSILON is also generally too small to catch accumulated floating-point error from the summed weighted similarities.
findings.suggestedFix: Use CORROBORATED_TIE_EPSILON consistently for all floating-point comparisons in this module, including the modularity gain comparison.

findings.title: No tests for key relaxed-merge boundary mechanisms
findings.description: The new tests cover the 3-reviewer happy path, the 2-reviewer rejection, claim-kind separation, and order determinism, but none exercise: (a) the 2-core peeling (a chain A—B—C of weak edges should not merge), (b) the density gate CORROBORATED_MIN_DENSITY, (c) fringe attachment via attachmentEvidence including the single-anchor + fixSupport escape hatch, (d) mergeAnchoredCommunities anchor-based merging, or (e) opposing-sentiment rejection on the relaxed path. Given the complexity of the new ~600-line clustering pipeline, these internal gates are effectively untested outside the fixture corpus.
findings.suggestedFix: Add unit tests for the 2-core/chain case (three findings where only sequential pairs are similar), a density-failure case, and at least one fringe-attachment case with two supporting reviewer assignments.

findings.title: Negative-guard consensus assertion may pass vacuously if concept fragments further
findings.description: For miningProxyOvermerged cases, the second test asserts each mustStaySeparate title's group scores below minConsensusScore. If the deduper regresses and splits a concept into many tiny groups, this test still passes (smaller groups score lower), and the first test also passes (groups are trivially separate). Nothing pins a lower bound on group size or membership for the negative case, so an under-merge regression in these fixtures is invisible.
findings.suggestedFix: Additionally assert each mustStaySeparate group's expected member titles (or a minimum member count) so both over-merge and under-merge regressions are caught.

findings.title: miningProxyOvermerged fixture flag validated at test-run time, not load time
findings.description: The requirement that miningProxyOvermerged implies mustStaySeparate is enforced by throwing inside individual `it` bodies. A malformed fixture fails with a generic thrown Error mid-test rather than being rejected when the corpus is loaded, and the check is duplicated in both tests. Consider validating fixture shape once (e.g., in a beforeAll or a schema check) so all fixture-contract violations surface uniformly.
findings.suggestedFix: Validate the CorpusCase invariants in a single load-time assertion loop over `corpus` instead of duplicating throws inside test bodies.

findings.title: corroborationTokens recomputed repeatedly for the same findings
findings.description: corroborationTokens, tokenize/jaccard computations, and conceptAnchors are recomputed many times for the same finding across relaxedLocationDuplicate, relaxedLocationWeight (which calls relaxedLocationDuplicate and then recomputes the same three similarities), groupsRelaxedWeight (all-pairs), attachmentEvidence, and mergeAnchoredCommunities. For N groups this is O(N^2) tokenizations of identical strings. relaxedLocationWeight in particular computes jaccardSimilarity(a.title, b.title) twice per pair (once inside the duplicate check, once for the weight).
findings.suggestedFix: Memoize token sets per finding (e.g., a WeakMap<Finding, Set<string>>) and have relaxedLocationWeight receive the precomputed similarities from relaxedLocationDuplicate instead of recomputing them.

findings.title: Community optimization cannot split a node into a singleton
findings.description: After removing a node from its current community, the candidate set contains only neighboring community labels and the current label. It does not include an empty/singleton community with insertion gain zero. If the calculated gain for returning to the current community is negative, separating the node may improve modularity, but this implementation is forced to put it into an existing community. Since these communities are the main over-merge boundary, this can retain lexical bridge nodes and incorrectly combine distinct findings.
findings.suggestedFix: Include a singleton candidate when evaluating moves, or compute each candidate's gain relative to restoring the current community and allow the node to remain isolated when that is the best option. Prefer a tested Louvain/community-detection implementation and add a regression graph where a previously merged node must split back out.

findings.title: Same reviewer can supply multiple independent core links
findings.description: The 2-core degree and edge-density calculations operate on strict finding groups, not distinct model-role assignments. A single reviewer can have multiple dissimilar strict groups because collapseSameReviewer is applied separately to each strict group. Those groups can then create multiple relaxed edges and satisfy another group's degree-of-two requirement, even though both links come from the same reviewer assignment. The later distinctReviewers >= 3 check only counts reviewers anywhere in the component and does not ensure that each core node has independent reviewer support, allowing one reviewer to disproportionately create a corroborated merge.
findings.suggestedFix: Build corroboration degree from distinct neighboring model-role assignments, ignoring or coalescing edges from the same assignment before computing the core and density. Add a test where two relaxed groups from one reviewer connect findings from two other reviewers but those other findings do not corroborate each other.

findings.title: Missing fallback for optional description causes false 'undefined' anchor token
findings.description: In `attachmentEvidence`, `singleton.finding.description` is interpolated directly into a template string without a fallback (`?? ''`). If `description` is `undefined`, JavaScript coerces it to the literal string `"undefined"`. `corroborationTokens` will extract `"undefined"` as a valid token (since it is not in `CORROBORATION_STOPWORDS`), causing findings with undefined descriptions to falsely match on the shared token `"undefined"`.

findings.title: corroborationFieldSimilar contradicts its own identifier-safety comment
findings.description: The comment states that a shared code identifier alone is only evidence that findings discuss the same function, not the same defect. However, the fallback `shared.length >= 2` returns true when the only shared tokens are two underscore-containing identifiers (e.g. `trigger_label` and `column_name`), which is exactly the false semantic edge the tokenization comment above warns about. Two findings about different defects in the same function that happen to mention two shared identifiers will pass this gate.
findings.suggestedFix: Require at least one non-identifier token unconditionally, e.g. `return shared.some((token) => !token.includes('_'));`, or count identifier matches separately with a higher bar (e.g. >= 3) that is documented as intentional.

findings.title: O(n²) relaxed-weight pass recomputes tokenization for every group pair
findings.description: agreementClusters computes groupsRelaxedWeight for every pair of strict groups across the entire result set, and each call re-tokenizes titles/descriptions/fixes via jaccardSimilarity/nonEmptyFieldSimilarity/corroborationTokens. relaxedLocationWeight short-circuits on file mismatch, but only after corroboration-independent work is avoided — actually the file check is first, so cross-file pairs are cheap, but same-file corpora with many findings will pay quadratic tokenization cost with no caching. groupTagged already had to solve this pairwise problem; consider bucketing strict groups by file before the pairwise pass and memoizing token sets per finding.
findings.suggestedFix: Pre-group strictGroups by finding.file before building the weight matrix, and cache corroborationTokens/tokenize results per finding id in a Map reused across relaxedLocationWeight, conceptAnchors, and attachmentEvidence.

findings.title: Domain-specific claim-kind regexes hardcoded in generic deduper
findings.description: TYPE_CONTRACT_PATTERN (@spec, typespec), GLOBAL_LOG_CAPTURE_PATTERN (capture_log), etc. are Elixir/Phoenix-specific heuristics embedded directly in the language-agnostic consensus deduper. These patterns silently do nothing for other ecosystems and will drift as new false-merge families are discovered. At minimum they deserve a comment noting they are calibrated to the RCL-17 corpus; ideally they would be configurable per-project.
findings.suggestedFix: Move the claim-kind patterns into a configurable list (e.g. passed via thresholds/options) or document them as corpus-calibrated constants with a pointer to the fixture README.

findings.title: mergeAnchoredCommunities is O(n³) worst-case with full re-sort per merge
findings.description: Each successful merge re-sorts the entire `remaining` array and restarts the outer scan from index 0 (`break outer`). With k clusters and m merges this is O(m · k log k · k) compatibility checks, each of which is itself quadratic in members via clustersAreCompatible and the hasCrossEdge flat() scans. Fine for the small corpus sizes tested, but the nested `target.groups.flat().some(... candidate.groups.flat().some(...))` inside the loop recomputes flat() arrays on every iteration.
findings.suggestedFix: Hoist `candidate.groups.flat()` out of the `some` callback (`const candidateMembers = candidate.groups.flat()`), and consider restarting the scan only from index i rather than re-sorting and restarting from 0.

findings.title: clustersShareFile rejects attachment when file sets are not exactly equal
findings.description: clustersShareFile requires `filesA.size === filesB.size` and mutual containment. A fringe candidate whose findings all sit in file X can never attach to a corroborated cluster that legitimately spans files X and Y (e.g. a fix touching a call site and its definition), even when every member of the candidate has strong evidence against the cluster. The equal-size requirement is stricter than the stated intent of 'same location' and will silently drop valid attachments.
findings.suggestedFix: Relax to subset containment in the direction that matters: `[...filesA].every((file) => filesB.has(file))`, or gate attachment on per-member areSameFile/linesOverlap evidence (which attachmentEvidence already enforces) and drop the file-set equality pre-filter.

findings.title: Determinism test only permutes review order, not finding order within reviews
findings.description: The determinism test reverses the array of three single-finding reviews. This exercises review-order stability but not order dependence among multiple findings inside one review, nor ties in the Louvain/attachment tie-break paths (CORROBORATED_TIE_EPSILON, compareAgreementClusters). The tricky ordering code (mergeAnchoredCommunities re-sort, attachment rounds) is exactly where order-dependence bugs would hide.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a case with several findings per review and shuffle both the reviews array and the findings within each review, asserting identical group signatures across permutations.

findings.title: Fringe attachment bypasses cluster-wide location compatibility
findings.description: Candidate targets are filtered only by file-set and claim-kind compatibility. Although attachmentEvidence requires each candidate member to overlap at least some target members, it does not require every candidate group to be location-compatible with every target group. A candidate can therefore attach at one edge of a corroborated cluster while being outside lineWindow for members at the other edge; later attachment rounds can extend this chain further. This can merge distinct nearby defects and violates the all-pairs location invariant enforced elsewhere by clustersAreCompatible.
findings.suggestedFix: Require cluster-wide location compatibility when selecting attachment targets, for example replace the clustersShareFile/clustersClaimsAreCompatible checks with `clustersAreCompatible(candidate.groups, target.groups, lineWindow)`. Add a regression test where a fringe finding overlaps only one edge of a cluster but is farther than lineWindow from another member.

findings.title: Louvain-style clustering is O(n²) and may struggle with large finding sets
findings.description: The `agreementClusters` function computes pairwise weights for all groups (O(n²)) and then runs a Louvain-style algorithm with up to `count * 2` passes (line 730), each iterating over all nodes and their neighbors. For large numbers of findings (e.g., 10k), this could be slow. Consider optimizing or documenting the expected input size.
findings.suggestedFix: If the number of findings can be large, consider limiting the clustering to smaller subsets or using a more efficient algorithm. Otherwise, document the expected input size.

findings.title: Attachment loop may not terminate if clusters change
findings.description: The attachment loop in `mergeCorroboratedLocationClusters` runs up to `CORROBORATED_MAX_ATTACHMENT_ROUNDS` times, but if attachments modify clusters in ways that create new candidates, the loop may not fully converge. While bounded, this could leave some fringe clusters unattached.
findings.suggestedFix: Ensure the loop either converges or document why a fixed number of rounds is sufficient.

findings.title: Overly strict separation check may fail for legitimate overlaps
findings.description: The test asserts that `leftGroup` and `rightGroup` are different (`expect(leftGroup).not.toBe(rightGroup)`), but does not check if they share any members. If the groups are separate but share some findings, the test would pass incorrectly.
findings.suggestedFix: Add an assertion to ensure the groups have no overlapping members.

findings.title: Documentation could clarify the role of `ao-7467-r1` as a negative guard
findings.description: The README mentions `ao-7467-r1` as a negative guard but does not explain why it was chosen or how it differs from the positive cases. Adding more context would help future maintainers.
findings.suggestedFix: Expand the explanation of why `ao-7467-r1` is a negative guard and what it tests.
